svg.title: DP-900 SQL management choices — practice exercise
svg.desc: DP-900. Practice version. Who runs which SQL layer? Three equal columns compare responsibility, not a universal product ranking. Read each stack downward: app/data/access, SQL platform, guest OS, Azure infrastructure. The app/data/access layer represents decisions, not application hosting inside the SQL service. The dashed line marks the shift to Microsoft-managed platform layers: after the first row for the two PaaS services, after the guest OS for the VM. Azure SQL Database. PaaS · database scope. Customer: application, data and access decisions. Microsoft: SQL engine platform upkeep and guest operating system. No customer guest OS access. Microsoft: Azure infrastructure. Database-oriented app. Check required SQL features. Azure SQL Managed Instance. PaaS · instance scope. Customer: application, data and access decisions. Microsoft: SQL engine platform upkeep and guest operating system. No customer guest OS access. Microsoft: Azure infrastructure. Instance-level dependencies. Check exact compatibility. SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines. IaaS · OS + SQL control. Customer: application, data and access decisions. Customer: SQL installation and engine; guest OS and added agents. Microsoft: Azure infrastructure. Guest OS + installation control. Own admin; automation can help. In every option the customer owns recovery requirements. Managed backups do not choose business recovery needs. Customers retain database administration, application/data/access decisions, workload tuning and security decisions. VM automation can help with patching, backup and availability. Three original, invented requirements follow. A / NEW APPLICATION. A compatible cloud app needs one database, with no instance-level or guest OS dependency. Choose a candidate, explain one tradeoff and identify a check before deployment. B / EXISTING SQL WORKLOAD. A migration needs instance-level SQL features and managed OS upkeep. No OS agent needed. Choose a candidate, explain one tradeoff and identify a check before deployment. C / VENDOR REQUIREMENT. The vendor requires a guest OS agent and control over the SQL Server installation. Choose a candidate, explain one tradeoff and identify a check before deployment. These are candidates to evaluate. VERIFY CURRENT: exact feature compatibility, vendor support and recovery configuration. Independent AI-assisted draft; human review pending. Selected objective only; accepted baseline July 21, 2026. The official DP-900 study guide is authoritative. Sources: Microsoft Learn Azure SQL comparison and DP-900 study guide. See the README for exact links and a separate answer section. No live Azure execution or vendor validation is claimed.

g.text: Match responsibilities to the workload; app hosting is a separate choice.
Start with the control you need
Own database administration, app/data/access decisions and recovery needs.
Platform upkeep does not remove workload tuning or security decisions.
Choose a candidate. Explain one tradeoff.
A compatible cloud app needs one database,
with no instance-level or guest OS dependency.
A migration needs instance-level SQL features
and managed OS upkeep. No OS agent needed.
The vendor requires a guest OS agent and
control over the SQL Server installation.
